 Overview of Duane Arnold Energy Center


• Duane Arnold Energy Center (DAEC) was designed
  as a single-unit boiling water reactor (BWR).
• DAEC shut down in 2020 due to market conditions.
  Restart is planned for Q1 2029.
• The current rated core thermal power is 1,912
  MWt, producing a gross electrical output of
  approximately 610 MWe.
• No refurbishment associated with the SLR is
  expected.

 Overview of Duane Arnold Energy Center


• Property within the site boundary comprises
  approximately 500 acres.
• The plant’s exclusion area boundary is defined by
  the site property line, which is about 2,000 feet
  from the reactor center point at its nearest point.
• DAEC is bounded by a 6-mile low population zone
  consistent with NRC siting regulations.

 Environmental Report Lessons Learned


• Incorporate lessons learned from previously submitted ERs into the DAEC SLR ER:
 • Early Coordination with Agencies
 • Alternatives Analysis
• Review and incorporate applicable information into the DAEC SLR ER based on previous NRC LR/SLR ER (as well as
  the DAEC ER prepared for the restart) Requests for Additional Information (RAIs) and Requests for Confirmation of
  Information (RCIs).
• Allocate sufficient time to test Information Technology (IT) resources and for the NRC to access the portal in
  support of the SLR ER audit.
